transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has arrived in Manila.
He's kicked off a short visit with allies at the ASEAN summit.
Tomorrow he heads to China for another summit and a historic meeting with two world leaders
and adversaries.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram has more.
Trump arrived on the tarmac in Manila with a big ceremony in a band that played YMCA,
ASEAN's signature to Trump's rallies.
The president met with leaders from India, Japan and Australia in an effort to bolster
the U.S.'s relationship with democracies in the Pacific region.
Tomorrow, Trump will travel to Shenzhen, China.
He's scheduled to attend an economic summit and meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, the
third meeting the two will have this year.
He and Xi will also meet together with Russian leader Vladimir Putin, marking the first time
these three leaders have met together.
Deepa Shivaram and PR News, Shenzhen.
The Pan American Health Organization is expected to announce today the U.S. has lost its measles
elimination status.
The U.S. has confirmed more than 5,400 cases so far this year and at least 10 deaths.
NPR's Maria Godoy reports officials say childhood measles vaccination rates are falling to a
level that is not enough to stop community outbreaks of the disease.
On a practical level, we're going to have to make sure that doctors know how to spot
measles and treat things not seen in generations like measles in pregnancy, and we're also
going to face increased costs for public health systems, more hospitalizations.
So we're going to have to find the political will and really fight to get vaccination rates
back up.
NPR's Maria Godoy reporting.
A new study shows large data centers are driving a major increase in planet heating emissions,
and PR's Julia Simon reports these rose dramatically last year.
The study looked at about 400 large U.S. data centers and estimated their electricity consumption
and carbon dioxide emissions.
The team, led by researchers at Harvard University, found the nation's largest data centers used
about 2 percent of the country's electricity, more than Los Angeles and New York combined.
Most of the electricity for data centers came from fossil fuels like natural gas and coal.
Data center growth is one reason that U.S. greenhouse gas emissions rose last year, according
to a recent U.N. report.
The U.S. sticks out as the only major economy where planet warming pollution increased dramatically
last year.
Julia Simon, NPR News.
The federal government is going to conduct a nationwide test today of its emergency alert
system.
This will include TV, radio, and satellite providers, but it will not include your cell
phone.
The emergency test will start at 2.20 p.m. Eastern time, which means at 11.20 a.m. Pacific
time.
Regular programming will be interrupted for the test.
No action or response are needed by the public.
This is NPR.
President Trump will meet Xi Jinping this week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific
Economic Summit in China.
The U.S. and China are in the midst of an AI race, but they're also competing on numerous
other fronts, including in mineral-rich Africa.
NPR's Kate Bartlett reports from Johannesburg.
China is, by far, Africa's biggest trading partner, and now more and more African countries
are turning to the Chinese yuan for trade and to pay their debt.
Christian Gérôt-Nima is an editor with the China Global South Project, an Africa-based
think tank which tracks Beijing's influence across the continent.
He points out several African countries, like Kenya, have already restructured their debt
to China and are now paying it in yuan rather than dollars.
When you have China as your main trade partner, it really just makes sense for many African
countries now to starting to trade with China in renminbi instead of trading with China
in U.S. dollar.
The Trump administration's shifting tariff policies have only strengthened the case for
African businesses to diversify away from the dollar.
Kate Bartlett, NPR News, Johannesburg.
Computer chipmaker NVIDIA is establishing a board committee.
Members will review national security and company compliance with global trade.
This move comes after former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair.
Reports suggest that was with a woman who was recruited to spy by China.
China has sought NVIDIA's powerful computer chips for its AI efforts.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Trump arrives in Manila for ASEAN summit, then heads to China for Xi and Putin meeting
Pan American Health Organization expected to declare U.S. has lost measles elimination status
Study finds large U.S. data centers drove sharp rise in planet-heating emissions last year
Federal government to test nationwide emergency alert system on TV, radio, and satellite
